transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I'm here because my sleep has basically just fallen apart. I'll lie in bed in my apartment for hours, my laptop is closed, but I'm still mentally rechecking everything—work deadlines, tuition payments, my class assignments. It just keeps going. And even when I finally do get some sleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off at all.
Do you find it difficult to fall asleep because your mind keeps racing with thoughts about things like work, school, or bills?

Yes, exactly. My mind just keeps jumping around. I'll worry about whether I’m falling behind at work, and then it shifts to whether I’m wasting money on school, or... or whether my family will think I just can’t handle things. I end up treating every small issue like it's this massive problem that could completely derail my whole future.
Have these sleep and anxiety problems been going on for a while, or did they start around a specific stressful event or change in your life?

It's been going on for a while, actually. I'd say it's been about a year and three months now. That was right around the time I started an evening graduate certificate program... while still trying to keep up with my full-time job as an analyst. So, yeah, taking on both of those at once is really when all this started.
Do you find your mind racing and feeling this level of worry during the day as well, or does it seem to mostly happen at night when you're trying to sleep?

It's definitely during the day, too. I'll try to tell myself to just stop and focus on one thing, but... it doesn't really work. One worry immediately leads to another. Before I know it, I'm checking my calendar, and then my budget, and my class assignments over and over again. I just get stuck in that loop instead of actually getting anything done.
Do you notice any physical symptoms during the day, like feeling restless, being easily fatigued, or having tense muscles, especially when you're worrying?

Yeah, I definitely notice the fatigue. By midafternoon at the office, I just feel completely drained. It gets to the point where even doing small things, like answering emails or just walking to the subway, takes so much effort. And... resting on the weekend doesn't even seem to give me my energy back. I just feel exhausted all the time.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about various things throughout the day, even when there isn’t an immediate deadline or specific problem to solve?

Yeah, all the time. There doesn't even need to be an immediate deadline or a real problem right in front of me. My mind just keeps jumping around. I'll worry about whether I’m falling behind at work... and then that turns into worrying about whether I’m just wasting money on school. Then I start stressing about my family, and if they think I can’t handle things. It's just constant. I basically treat every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future.
Do you feel like you’re unable to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might be excessive or unnecessary?

Yeah, it really feels impossible to control. Like I mentioned a little bit ago... I'll literally tell myself to just stop and focus on one single thing, but it doesn't work. One worry just immediately feeds into the next one. Even when I know I'm being excessive, I still end up in that loop of checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over again. I just can't shut it off so I can actually get my work done.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?

Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or sad. I still want to see my friends and do my normal hobbies... it's just that, like I said earlier, I'm usually too exhausted or too stressed out to actually go out and do them. But I definitely haven't lost interest. I just don't have the mental energy for it right now.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or staying focused on tasks because of all the worrying and mental exhaustion?

Yes, definitely. It happens a lot. I’ll just... sit there and stare at the same financial model for work, or a reading for my classes, for ages. I'll realize I’ve reread the exact same paragraph like five times and haven't absorbed a single word of it. I just can't focus because my head is already off running through everything else that could go wrong.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things in your life, even when there isn’t a clear or immediate problem to solve?

Yeah, definitely. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to the next. Like, I'll be worrying about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then it immediately shifts to whether I'm wasting my money on school... or if my family is going to think I can't handle everything. It's just constant. I basically treat every single small issue like it could completely derail my entire future, even when there isn't actually a real problem to solve yet.
Has this constant worrying and mental exhaustion significantly affected your ability to function in your job, school, or personal relationships?

Yeah, it really has. Um, at work, I've actually started missing deadlines recently, which is really frustrating. And I'm falling behind in my certificate classes, too. I just... I can't seem to keep up with it all right now. And outside of work and school, I've completely stopped doing the daily routines that used to keep me grounded. Like, I used to do yoga, go running, and I liked cooking my own meals... but I just don't do any of that anymore. I just don't have it in me.
Have you been experiencing this constant worry and anxiety for more than six months?

Yeah, definitely more than six months. Um, I'd say it's been going on for about a year and three months now. It pretty much started right when I began my evening graduate certificate program... while still trying to keep up with my full-time analyst job.
